cosine_findings.headline: Trust and Cooperation are roughly orthogonal at mean_trace (mean cos -0.13) but moderately aligned at last_trace (mean cos +0.51). They share output-space basis but diverge during reasoning.

steering_findings.headline: Applying the trust vector at PD-tuned layers (16, 25) on E4B yields WEAK steering: 12-26 pp dose-response range vs PD coop's 58 pp at the same cell. Direction is sometimes inverted (more alpha -> less trust at L16). Confirms the cosine result: PD-effective layers do not transfer to trust steering. A trust-tuned layer scan is needed.

calibration_curve_findings.headline: Gemma 4 E4B is NOT calibrated to trust-game payoff structure. Across all 10 cells (n=23-29 each), trust rate hovers at 33-52% regardless of the break-even betrayal probability p*. Cooperation prior dominates EV reasoning.
calibration_curve_findings.data_source: Per-cell baseline (α=0) from the 252-story train-extract index.parquet. Replaces an earlier reading from the 50-story eval subset that had n=2-10 per cell and produced misleadingly steep cell-level rates.

users_specific_games.implication: Despite Game B having 5x the breakeven probability of Game A (0.10 vs 0.50), E4B trusts at nearly the same rate in both (~40%). The model is responding to narrative framing rather than to the payoff structure.

summary_statistics.interpretation: Standard deviation across cells is ~0.06; the curve is essentially flat.

takeaways_for_paper: Trust is a mechanistically distinct direction from cooperation at mean_trace (cos ~0) - confirms procedural CAA methodology yields multiple axes.
Trust is NOT effectively steered by PD-tuned layers - direct evidence that the useful steering layer is concept-specific, not just model-specific.
E4B is NOT EV-calibrated on trust games: trust rate is ~40% across 10 cells spanning p* in [0.02, 0.95]. The cooperation prior dominates the payoff structure.

The trust direction at last_trace partially aligns with cooperation (+0.51) - by the time the model emits the decision, prosocial intent collapses into a shared subspace. Reasoning-time representations diverge.
The user's two specific games (Game A: classic_trust_game; Game B: asymmetric_loss) yield ~38% and ~42% trust respectively - a 4 pp difference despite a 5x ratio in breakeven betrayal probability.
